questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Milan because it is a beautiful city, and because I love Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit hard to find out what should be done and when - I received a lot of emails, but it was hard to know when I needed to do something. The many emails were very confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We did not receive any information on how we could find the timetable, exam dates etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard, since most tenancies could only be rented for a minimum of two or four years. It was pretty expensive too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The rental is expensive, and it is hard to find a proper rental for students to pay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go to the Erasmus office and they had to sign the proof of attendance. Then we had to register for the subjects we wanted. This was a bit difficult, as it was difficult to see when the individual subjects had classes, and as it was not possible to see when the exam was. It was therefore difficult to draw up a schedule. At last we had to register for the exam, which I also found difficult, because you could only register for oral exams, and it was not made clear how to register for written exams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As far as i know there was no help to be had anywhere. I think you could go to the Erasmus office, but in general I don't think there was much help to be had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful. I did not get any of the classes that I wanted in the first place. Many of the subjects I had initially chosen, I suddenly couldn't choose, and the classes were on top of each other in the subjects I could choose.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't expect to get any of the classes you want in the first place, as they may not be available after all. Also, expect to spend quite some time, to choose the classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was actually not satisfied with the academic programme, as I think it was very uncoordinated.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses were very low. We did not have to read anything through the semester, and overall, the teachers did not expect much from us. Furthermore the exams were quite unorganized and loose.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very loose! AT UCPH they are a lot more coordinated and structured.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Access to justice in a multilevel constitutional system
Law and policies of social rights protection in Europe
Competiton law and economics
Comparative Labour law
Smart cities, artificial intelligence and digital transformation law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Smart cities, artificial intelligence and digital transformation law was a very nice course and had an easy written exam.

questions.answer: I did now expect to use that many money on food. Groceries were very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus hosted a lot of events for other exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Watch a football match at San Siro, walk up the Duomo, Go to the Prada Museom, Brera-museum and the botanical garden in Brera.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit lake Como (including the beautiful city Bellagio). Also visit Bergamo, Crema, Verona, Rome and Genova.
Watch a football match at San Siro

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the local students in class, as you may not see each other outside of school.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find it challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I kind of liked how loose the Italians were, including their way of hosting an exam.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You can expect to spend a lot of time choosing and coordinating your classes. 
The exams can be held in different ways, and you can not know in advance when these will take place.
You need to get an italian tax-code (codice fiscale) !!! it may be hard to get, but you will need it in many ways.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need a tax code!! (codice fiscale)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of new friends from my own country, as we were a lot of danish exchange students in Milan. I also learned (from having two or three exam per week) that I should not stress that much about an exam - I just need to trust that I have done my best, based on the time we had to prepare for the exams.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The planning and scheduling - we constantly had to plan and schedule everything (including exams as we did not know in advantage when these would take place) and it was a bit stressful.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
